Let $\Omega$ be a [[sample space]], $\mathcal{F}(X)$ be any of its [[sigma algebra]], then

$$
(\Omega,\mathcal{F}(X))
$$

is a [[measure space]], where $F \in \mathcal{F}(X)$ are '''events''' to which [[measure]]s can be assigned.

== Special case: Countable sample space ==

For [[cardinality|countable]] sample spaces, one usually takes

$$
\mathcal F=\mathcal P(\Omega),
$$
where $\mathcal{P}$ is the [[power set]] of $\Omega$.
